entries.summary: Identify this LHP project in generated resources and monitoring.
details: Choose a stable project name. This is project metadata, not the name of an individual pipeline or flowgroup.

entries.summary: Record the version of your project configuration.
details: This value describes your project; required_lhp_version controls the supported LHP installation versions.
entries.unsetBehavior: LHP uses the project model default, "1.0".
constraints: Keep the YAML value a string: quote numeric-looking versions.

entries.summary: Explain the purpose of this project to the people maintaining it.
details: Describe the datasets or business area it covers. This metadata does not change action processing.

entries.summary: Record who owns or maintains this project.
details: Use a team or author name that helps other contributors find the owner. This is descriptive metadata, not an access-control setting.

entries.summary: Record when the project was created.
details: Use a quoted date such as "2026-09-09" to keep it as text in YAML; it does not schedule pipeline execution.

entries.summary: Require a compatible LHP version before generating this project.
details: Use a PEP 440 version constraint. A range can allow compatible updates while excluding a breaking release.
entries.unsetBehavior: No project-level LHP version constraint is enforced.

entries.summary: Choose which flowgroup YAML files LHP discovers.
details: Patterns are relative to pipelines/. Use a directory pattern when a project contains several layers; do not add another pipelines/ prefix.

entries.summary: Choose which blueprint definitions LHP discovers.
details: These patterns select reusable blueprint definitions, not the instance files that supply values to them.

entries.summary: Choose where LHP discovers blueprint instance files.
details: Instance discovery distinguishes files by their content, so overlap with ordinary flowgroup discovery is safe.

entries.summary: Format generated Python after code generation.
details: The Python syntax validity check still runs when formatting is off. The CLI --no-format option overrides this project setting.

entries.summary: Add reusable audit columns to generated datasets.
details: Define each column once, group columns into metadata presets, then choose the default selection. Flowgroups and actions can select metadata explicitly.

entries.summary: Define the expressions used to populate audit columns.
details: Each mapping key becomes a column name. Use an object for expression, target types and imports, or a bare expression string for the short form.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
operational_metadata:
  columns:
    _processed_at:
      expression: F.current_timestamp()
      applies_to: [streaming_table, materialized_view]

entries.summary: Compute this metadata column for each row.
details: Use a Spark expression such as F.current_timestamp(). Declare any imports the expression needs in additional_imports.

entries.summary: Explain what this audit column records.
details: Describe its meaning so someone selecting metadata can distinguish processing time, source identity and business values.

entries.summary: Choose the dataset types that receive this metadata column.
details: Select only targets where the expression is valid. For example, file-source _metadata columns should be captured in the load view.
entries.unsetBehavior: The default target types are streaming_table and materialized_view.

entries.summary: Add imports needed by this column’s Spark expression.
details: Enter complete Python import statements. LHP includes them in generated code that uses the metadata expression.

entries.summary: Control whether this metadata column is available for generation.
details: Disable a column when it should not be added, while keeping its expression and documentation in the project.

entries.summary: Group audit columns into reusable named selections.
details: Each preset lists column names defined under operational_metadata.columns. This grouping is separate from an action configuration preset.

entries.summary: Select the audit columns included by this metadata preset.
details: Use existing column names; this list selects definitions rather than creating new expressions.

entries.summary: Explain when someone should choose this metadata preset.
details: Describe the purpose of the group, such as ingestion traceability or processing audit.

entries.summary: Choose metadata when a flowgroup does not make its own selection.
details: Use the documented metadata selection forms: a boolean, column selection or named preset selection. An explicit flowgroup/action selection may override this default.

entries.summary: Configure event-log tables used to inspect pipeline activity.
details: Enabling the block requires a catalog and schema. Naming prefixes and suffixes let each pipeline have its own event-log table.

entries.summary: Enable project event-log configuration for generated pipelines.
details: Monitoring depends on event logging being enabled. Individual pipelines may explicitly override or disable their event log.

entries.summary: Choose the catalog that stores pipeline event logs.
details: Required while event logging is enabled. Substitution tokens resolve for the selected generation environment.

entries.summary: Choose the schema that stores pipeline event logs.
details: Required while event logging is enabled; keep event-log storage separate from business tables when that matches your project layout.

entries.summary: Add a prefix before each pipeline’s event-log table name.
details: The pipeline name remains part of the table name, so logs from different pipelines can be distinguished.

entries.summary: Add a suffix after each pipeline’s event-log table name.
details: Use the suffix to follow your team’s event-log naming convention.

entries.summary: Combine pipeline event logs into monitoring datasets.
details: LHP generates a union notebook, a monitoring pipeline and a workflow connecting them. Enable event logging and provide checkpoint_path and job_config_path first.

entries.summary: Generate the project’s monitoring workflow.
details: Requires enabled event logging, a checkpoint location and a monitoring job config path.

entries.summary: Name the pipeline that builds monitoring views.
details: Choose a name distinct from business pipelines; without an override LHP derives it from the project name.

entries.summary: Choose the catalog for monitoring tables.
details: When omitted, monitoring uses the event-log catalog.

entries.summary: Choose the schema for monitoring tables.
details: When omitted, monitoring uses the event-log schema.

entries.summary: Name the Delta table that receives the unified event-log streams.
details: The monitoring notebook writes pipeline event logs into this table; downstream monitoring views read from it.

entries.summary: Choose persistent storage for monitoring stream checkpoints.
details: LHP creates a per-pipeline checkpoint subdirectory. This is required when monitoring is enabled; use a stable storage location.

entries.summary: Choose the YAML settings file for the monitoring job.
details: Use a project-relative path such as config/monitoring_job_config.yaml. It controls monitoring compute, schedule and notifications and is required when monitoring is enabled.

entries.summary: Limit how many event-log streams the union notebook runs at once.
details: This controls the notebook’s worker pool, not the number of business pipelines or concurrent workflow runs.

entries.summary: Also collect orchestration-job run information.
details: Adds job monitoring using the Databricks SDK and a jobs_stats materialized view, alongside pipeline event monitoring.

entries.summary: Define the views built over the unified event-log data.
details: Each view needs a name and either an inline SQL query or a SQL file reference.

entries.summary: Name this monitoring materialized view.
details: Choose a dataset name that communicates the metric or diagnostic it exposes.

entries.summary: Write the query for this monitoring view.
details: Provide inline SQL or sql_path, not both. Keep reusable or longer queries in a SQL file.

entries.summary: Load this monitoring view’s query from a SQL file.
details: Use a project-relative .sql path and remove the inline sql key when selecting a file.

entries.summary: Apply declared table and column tags to Unity Catalog.
details: Declaring tags opts a table into the generated tagging hook. The feature is enabled by default; this block controls the project-wide behavior.

entries.summary: Enable the hook that applies declared Unity Catalog tags.
details: Set false to disable tag application across the project without removing tag declarations.
entries.unsetBehavior: Enabled by default, including when the entire uc_tagging block is absent.

entries.summary: Remove existing tags that are absent from the declared YAML.
details: Enable this only when the YAML should own the complete tag set. It can remove tags set by other tools or people.
entries.unsetBehavior: False: existing undeclared tags are retained.

entries.summary: Limit parallel tag operations in the generated hook.
details: Choose an integer from 1 to 20. Lower values reduce concurrent requests when applying tags.

entries.summary: Set how many consecutive failures the tagging hook tolerates.
details: A nonnegative integer supplies the hook’s failure budget. Explicit null means no limit, so the hook is never disabled by that budget.

entries.summary: Publish test results through a project-provided Python hook.
details: Provide the module and function implementing your reporter. An optional YAML config file supplies reporter settings.

entries.summary: Choose the Python file implementing test-result reporting.
details: Use the project’s original module, not a generated copy. Pair it with function_name to identify the report hook.

entries.summary: Name the report hook inside the Python module.
details: The function must implement the documented reporting interface; selecting a name does not verify external delivery.

entries.summary: Supply optional YAML settings to the report hook.
details: Use this for reporter configuration that should live separately from the hook implementation.

entries.summary: Configure where wheel-packaged pipeline artifacts are uploaded.
details: Only pipelines using packaging: wheel consume this setting. Source packaging does not require an artifact volume.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog volume path for built wheels.
details: Substitution tokens resolve per environment. The resolved path must begin with /Volumes/; required when any pipeline uses wheel packaging.

entries.summary: Set the team policy for developer sandbox generation.
details: This shared policy lives in lhp.yaml. A developer’s personal namespace lives in the separate local profile.

entries.summary: Choose how generated sandbox tables are isolated.
details: Only table renaming is implemented. Catalog and schema isolation strategies are not available.

entries.summary: Build sandbox table names from the namespace and original table name.
details: Include both {namespace} and {table}. Literal text may contain letters, digits and underscores; format specifiers and conversions are not supported.

entries.summary: Limit sandbox generation to named environments.
details: Use the names of environments configured by your project. An empty list is invalid; remove the key to allow all environments.
